summary: Octagonal brick light of 1888 on Pipe Island in the St. Marys River, Michigan; privately owned, closed, and best seen from the water.

light.characteristic: fixed red then flashing white (see events)

lens.note: Fifth-order Henry-Lepaute Fresnel (LighthouseFriends); USLHS lists the current optic as a lens lantern.

structures.type: octagonal brick tower with cast-iron lantern
structures.note: LighthouseFriends gives 32.5 ft; USLHS gives 27 ft to lantern centre.

staffing.note: Last keeper on the roster is James Brander (1937-1948); no later staffing found.

access.note: Privately owned; grounds, dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Best seen from the water.

events.note: Congress appropriated $10,000 for a light on Pipe Island (3 March 1885); deed finalized 2 November 1885 (LighthouseFriends).
Octagonal buff brick tower on a cut-limestone foundation with keeper's dwelling and boathouse; buildings completed 8 December 1887 per the Board's 1888 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends.
Lighted on the night of 12 May 1888 with a fifth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends).
Oil house and 1,200 bricks delivered to the station; act of 3 March 1891 appropriated $30,000 for lights and ranges from Pipe Island to Sault Ste. Marie.
Tower paint changed from red to white so it could serve as a day mark with Frying Pan Island light (Board's report for the year to 30 June 1894).

Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1897 says the Detour range lights on Frying Pan and Pipe Island should be increased in power and Pipe Island made a flashing light; both then fixed red, fifth and sixth order.
Keeper Frank Bernard died at the station on 25 August 1910 (LighthouseFriends).
Steamers Pentecost Mitchell (down-bound with ore) and Saxona (up-bound) collided at night in fog; both sank in about 40 feet; crews saved; both later raised (newspapers; LighthouseFriends).
Lighthouse Bureau placed two spar buoys with red lights to mark an alternate channel on the other side of Pipe Island (LighthouseFriends).
Pipe Island listed among lights established as flashing white, lens lantern, acetylene (Lighthouse Service Bulletin).

Focal plane raised to 52 ft on 21 October 1920 from a 15-ft skeleton tower; light returned to fixed red on 17 November (LighthouseFriends). Commissioner's report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1920 lists one appropriation for changing the light to nonattended acetylene.
Work at Pipe Island and Frying Pan Island completed in the fiscal year ended June 30, 1921 (Commissioner's report).
Keeper Norman P. Hawkins died in April 1937, after about twenty years at the station (LighthouseFriends; roster).
Changed to an electric light producing two red flashes every five seconds; LighthouseFriends says it was then listed as unwatched, though Brander kept the station until 1948.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends gives the tower as 32.5 ft (9.9 m). The record's 8.2 m comes from Wikidata; USLHS gives 27 ft to the lantern centre, so the figure is itself uncertain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the repainting to 1895. The Light-House Board's report for the year to 30 June 1894 already records the change, so 1894 is the earliest date the sources support.

notes_for_editor: Status is disputed. The USLHS record says not an active aid to navigation; the record's Wikidata entry says active. The Coast Guard Light List (Great Lakes volume VII) was not read: the fetch timed out. The 1888 first-light and 1887 completion dates rest on LighthouseFriends quoting the Board's 1888 report, which is not in the local corpus. The 1917 collision location differs: the 1917 newspapers say at the mouth of the St. Marys River at midnight; LighthouseFriends says near Pipe Island in fog. Both are reported in the story. The 1920 'nonattended acetylene' wording in the Commissioner's report sits uneasily with keepers on the roster until 1948; reported, not resolved. Keeper Norman Hawkins's death certificate details in LighthouseFriends are deliberately left out (private family matter, not needed). Later private owners are not named (private persons). Only LighthouseFriends facts are used; the story quotes nothing from it beyond evidence fragments. Pipe Island tower height conflicts across sources (9.9 m LF, 8.2 m Wikidata, 27 ft USLHS to lantern centre). Corrections made by the fact-checker 2026-10-28: the 1896 Detour statement is in the Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1897 (scan page 420), and the 1891 act is at scan page 203. The story states the tower-height disagreement (LighthouseFriends 32.5 ft; USLHS 27 ft from base to lantern centre). The collision date and place differ between LighthouseFriends and the 1917 newspapers and the story says so.
